creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Unplugging a laptop and then relaunching Muster leaves every devenv pane dead, and relaunching again does not help. `a_2HrmSyRAQ` documents relaunching as "the whole recovery" for a dropped connection. It is not, when the drop and the relaunch happen in that order.

On 0.4.1, three devenv panes, network unplugged while Muster was running, Muster quit and reopened:

    muster-bridge: could not attach to pane w4:p2: terminal attach failed:
    terminal term_65a6bff3dab3da already has an attached client; retry with --takeover
    Process exited. Press any key to close the terminal.

All three panes, all three agents untouched behind them. `muster window` listed them correctly and `muster pane read` returned their contents throughout, because those go over the control socket. Only rendering was gone.

## What the far machine was holding

The previous app's ssh master survived the unplug on the devenv side, with its three bridge clients still attached:

    PID      PPID     ELAPSED  COMMAND
    1707967  87       31:53    sshd: aterp@notty
    1708967  1707967  31:50    herdr terminal session control w4:p2 --cols 164 --rows 27
    1708971  1707967  31:50    herdr terminal session control w4:p1 --cols 164 --rows 59
    1713704  1707967  30:25    herdr terminal session control w4:p3 --cols 164 --rows 29

No process on the laptop matched pid 1707967. Its near end died with the unplug and the far end never noticed, which is `a_2I76eCrjw`. The geometries are the old external-monitor layout, which is how they were identifiable as belonging to the app that had gone.

## Why the new app could not get past them

`~/Library/Logs/muster/muster-2026-09-01_09-02-11-44143.jsonl`, in order:

    14:02:14.246  bridge.start          w4:p3  takeover=false  rows=16
    14:02:14.249  bridge.start          w4:p1  takeover=false  rows=16
    14:02:14.254  bridge.start          w4:p2  takeover=false  rows=15
    14:02:14.251  pane.typeable         p2073ed9cw
    14:02:14.251  pane.typeable         p206y9p61r
    14:02:14.268  pane.typeable         p2072zszrh
    14:02:14.782  bridge.attach.failed  w4:p2  already has an attached client
    14:02:14.783  bridge.attach.failed  w4:p1  already has an attached client
    14:02:14.783  bridge.attach.failed  w4:p3  already has an attached client
    (nothing further)

`takeover=false` on all three is by design. `MusterWindow.swift:522` passes `reattaching: pane.bridgeRestarts > 0`, and `corpus/conformance/respawn.json` states the rule: "zero means this window has never had a bridge for this pane end, so its first one attaches plainly rather than taking a terminal some other window is legitimately showing." A freshly launched app has zero for every pane, so every attach after a relaunch is a plain one - and a plain attach is exactly what an orphan refuses.

## The respawn that should have covered this

Nothing follows those three refusals. No `pane.bridge.exited`, no respawn decision either way, though all three panes had logged `pane.typeable` half a second earlier. A working respawn would have recovered this on its own: the first replacement is `Start(1)`, and `bridgeRestarts > 0` makes that one a takeover.

That turned out to be the larger bug and is now `a_2IRcMjFs0` - no bridge that dies reaches the policy at all, in any scenario. If that one is fixed first, this card may need nothing further. What would still be open is the first-attach rule below, which only matters if a respawn is not available to supply the takeover.

## Recovering it by hand

Killing the three orphans on the devenv freed the terminals. Muster did not then retry, so a relaunch was still needed, and after one everything came back.

    ssh <host> 'pgrep -fa "herdr terminal session control"'   # find them
    ssh <host> 'kill -TERM <pids>'                            # release the terminals
    # then relaunch Muster

Safe because these are clients rather than terminals: the daemon owns the agents, and it had been running 20 hours across all of this.

## Fixing it

- **Make a refused attach reach the respawn path.** The narrow reading of the second finding above, and it fixes this case without touching the takeover rule. Find why `onProcessExited` did not fire for a bridge that failed to attach.
- **Retry with `--takeover` when the refusal says a client is already attached.** Narrower than taking over on every first attach, since the refusal names the state. The risk the corpus comment guards against stays real: another Muster window legitimately showing the pane would lose it. Muster cannot currently tell that window from an orphan, which is what `a_2I76eCrjw` is asking herdr for.
- **Neither, if the daemon releases the terminal.** `a_2I76eCrjw` upstream. That removes the orphan and nothing here needs to change.

## Validating a fix

- Reproduce: open remote panes, pull the network, quit Muster, restore the network, reopen. Every pane renders.
- The refused-attach path produces a respawn decision in the run log, whichever way it decides.
- A second Muster window opening onto a pane the first is rendering does not take it away. That is the property the plain first attach exists to protect, and any takeover change has to keep it.
title: 🔌 A relaunch cannot recover panes whose orphaned bridges outlived the last app
